sourceVariantTitle: The Convenient Virtue of the Perfect Consumer
scoreRule: One point per correct answer; ten points maximum. Provisional local result only.
description: Independent English C2 film-review comprehension bank requiring human pedagogical approval.

tabs.title: Evaluation
tabs.description: Apply the ideas to new situations.

questions.q: What is the central irony in the film's celebration of the teenager with the flask?
choices: The teenager's flask was made in the same factory as disposable cups.
The audience was not genuinely moved by the teenager's speech.
The institutional arrangements at the screening remain unexamined while individual virtue is applauded.
The venue had banned all private reusable containers.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1 of this C2 film criticism develops the stated argument; the competing interpretations omit or exaggerate relevant conditions.

questions.q: Why is immediately accusing the venue of hypocrisy 'satisfying and uninformative'?
choices: The venue has already published a complete impact study.
It delivers a moral verdict without examining the logistical limitations involved.
A critic cannot judge an institution's own policies.
It proves that all recycling plans are financially impossible.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 of this C2 film criticism develops the stated argument; the competing interpretations omit or exaggerate relevant conditions.

questions.q: How does the writer challenge the film's implied account of environmental causation?
choices: It assumes that people can never choose how to behave.
It claims public procurement has no relation to consumption.
It argues that narrative techniques prevent any environmental change.
It leaves out systems that make individual habits more or less effective.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 of this C2 film criticism develops the stated argument; the competing interpretations omit or exaggerate relevant conditions.

questions.q: Why would blaming governments alone give consumers an 'equally flattering absolution'?
choices: It releases private actors from considering their contribution to collective change.
It makes every consumer responsible for all public contracts.
It proves that purchasing habits cannot affect design decisions.
It requires citizens to act without any public support.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 4 of this C2 film criticism develops the stated argument; the competing interpretations omit or exaggerate relevant conditions.

questions.q: What does the hypothetical flask lost after one month illustrate?
choices: Metal is necessarily more harmful than every disposable material.
The only measure of sustainability is whether an object can be found.
A sustainable symbol must also be evaluated through manufacture, lifespan and actual use.
Any individual product can be assessed without considering its context.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 5 of this C2 film criticism develops the stated argument; the competing interpretations omit or exaggerate relevant conditions.

questions.q: What concession does the writer make to filmmakers who appeal to urgency?
choices: Emotional engagement matters, but it does not cancel the duty to describe uncertainty accurately.
Urgency makes all omissions morally acceptable.
A moving film should never include costs or measurements.
The time available for a decision has no effect on environmental action.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 6 of this C2 film criticism develops the stated argument; the competing interpretations omit or exaggerate relevant conditions.

questions.q: Why would a shot of a clipboard be more informative than another aerial coastline image?
choices: It would show that the entire trial had been free of problems.
It would reveal measurable returns, losses and questions for future revisions.
It would prove that the coastline would never become polluted.
It would remove the need to consult anyone who ran the event.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 6 of this C2 film criticism develops the stated argument; the competing interpretations omit or exaggerate relevant conditions.

questions.q: How does the example of students campaigning for drinking fountains complicate the individual-versus-system debate?
choices: It proves that schools are required to follow every student demand.
It demonstrates that public provision always comes before any private habit.
It suggests that students cannot influence the design of shared facilities.
It shows that private initiative and institutional provision can reinforce each other.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 4 of this C2 film criticism develops the stated argument; the competing interpretations omit or exaggerate relevant conditions.

questions.q: A deposit trial loses more cups than expected. What would constitute a responsible response?
choices: Reject the idea of reuse without making any measurements.
Investigate design, losses and costs rather than declaring instant triumph or failure.
Praise the scheme because a trial's costs do not matter.
Hide missing cups to keep the audience's enthusiasm.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 6 of this C2 film criticism develops the stated argument; the competing interpretations omit or exaggerate relevant conditions.

questions.q: What kind of audience does the writer ultimately hope environmental cinema will develop?
choices: One that can confidently declare itself morally innocent.
One that judges the quality of a film by its final scenic image.
One that accepts simple explanations without examining causation.
One capable of asking questions about missing actors, constraints and consequences.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 7 of this C2 film criticism develops the stated argument; the competing interpretations omit or exaggerate relevant conditions.
